utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is Case Number IT-98-34-T, the Prosecutor versus Naletilic and Martinovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I'm so glad you found your voice back. Well, Mr. Usher, would you please bring in the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can hear you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Sit down, please. Please remember that you are still under the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any cross-examination? Mr. Meek, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Cross-examined by Mr. Meek:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness ZZ. How are you this morning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm fine. Thank you. How about you?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Fine for a Monday morning. My name is Chris Meek, and I am one of the attorneys for Mr. Naletilic, and I will have a few questions for you based on what your testimony was Friday. Okay?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Your Honour, I seem to be having some problems with my microphone cutting in and out. I'll try another one. Mr. President, could we go into private session for a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We'll go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: ZZ, on the 10th day of May, 1993, you were on duty with the army ABiH as a military policeman in the Vranica building; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after the assault began on the early morning hours of the 9th of May, you stayed for approximately 36 hours before you were taken in to custody; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Afterwards, you were arrested by HVO soldiers; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you ended up going to a building called the ministry building. Is that a fact?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not into the building itself, but in front of the building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know today what the name of that ministry office is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not know its name even then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you do not know it today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I do not. I do not know it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You indicated that there were many HVO soldiers present; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you give me an estimate of approximately how many HVO soldiers were there, 100, 150?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean in front of the ministry?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, Witness.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, to be honest with you, I didn't even try counting them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So at this time, these many years later, you cannot even give us an estimate. Would that be a fair statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I could give you an estimate, but I wouldn't be able to tell you exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is your estimate, Witness ZZ?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe between 40 and 50 men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You indicated in your testimony that afterwards you were taken with a group of other Bosniaks to the MUP station in Siroki Brijeg. Was that on the same day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you indicated, I think, in your direct testimony that there were perhaps 50 to 60 of you taken to Siroki Brijeg MUP station. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would that be an estimate, again, an estimate such as you just gave me on the amount of soldiers, the number of soldiers who were present at the ministry building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could it have been as few as 40 in that group rather than 60?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if we have had other witnesses who were in that same group testify in this Tribunal that there were approximately 40 people total, and 17 to 20 per cell, they would be mistaken and you would be correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: To me, it seemed that there were more. I think that that was wrong. But it is possible, because even then, I did not think of counting them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You indicated in your direct testimony that when you were in the court yard or yard of the ministry building that you saw a man who you called "Tuta." Is that a fact?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you also said that you believe that this man that you saw named Tuta had some guards with him; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean in front of the ministry?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, Witness ZZ.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to make sure, because I am looking through my notes from your testimony, the reason you believe this man you saw had the name of Tuta was because you thought that because you had heard that these people were Tuta's guards; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, and I had seen Mr. Tuta before.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: May the witness be asked to speak closer to the microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear that, Witness ZZ? The interpreter asked that you speak closer to the microphone when you answer the questions.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Fine. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness ZZ, have you had an opportunity to review your four-page statement that you gave to the OTP back in 1998 prior to your testimony today and Friday?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall in that statement that you gave that you told OTP in 1998 that "I first saw Tuta in front of the ministry building."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that sentence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you mean by that sentence that this is the first time in Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. your life that you had seen Tuta?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I first saw Mr. Tuta, and I was sure that it was Mr. Tuta. It was the first time that I knew that it was Mr. Tuta.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the reason you knew it was Mr. Tuta is people told you that. Isn't that a fact?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your prior answer, ZZ, you stated that "No, I first saw Mr. Tuta, and I was sure that it was Mr. Tuta." Was that that day, on the 10th of May, that you were sure it was Mr. Tuta?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you tell me, please, when it was prior to the 10th day of May, 1993, that you had ever seen Mr. Tuta?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had seen him in some coffee shop, but I was not sure at the time that it was he.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you tell me, Witness ZZ, was this sighting an isolated incident?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean before? Yes, it had been the first time -- it was the first time that I had seen that gentleman.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was it the only time that you had seen that gentleman prior to the 10th of May, 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you give me an idea of how close in time it was to the 9th of May, 1993? Had it been six months, had it been one year, had it been two years? Do you have an idea today as to the approximate date that you had -- the first and only time you had seen Mr. Tuta before the 10th of May of 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I have no idea.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any idea as to the location or name of the cafe bar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot recall now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But it was only after the 10th day of May that people told you that this man was named Tuta; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is also correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And everything that you testified about on Friday concerning Tuta, that knowledge was gained from conversations you had with other people. Is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. Because I knew that gentleman only by his face.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And besides the single incident of a sighting of this gentleman in a cafe bar, you had never seen him, his picture, in magazines, newspapers, or on TV. Would that be a fair statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, I was not reading papers or watch television.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've testified last week, ZZ, that while you were in Siroki Brijeg at the MUP station, you had an occasion to observe or have another sighting of this individual, Mr. Tuta; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that occurred, did it not, on an occasion that you were working at the municipal swimming pool in Siroki Brijeg?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any recollection today, because I did not notice in your statement from 1998, how was Mr. Tuta dressed that day, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this is at Siroki Brijeg, at the swimming pool location I'm talking about.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, do you believe, Witness ZZ, that your memory was fresher on 25 November, 1998, when you spoke with the Office of the Prosecutor and gave your statement than it is today, in the year 2002?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that my memory is the same.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The reason I asked that is because on page 3 of the written statement you gave in 1998 to the Office of the Prosecutor, you indicated very specifically -- and I will show you the statement if you do not recall -- that on the occasion that you saw Mr. Tuta in Siroki Brijeg at the municipal pool, that he had arrived and stayed "only for a few minutes." Do you recall giving that statement in 1998?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Because I notice, Witness ZZ, that in your testimony on Friday in response to questions by Mr. Stringer, you indicated that Mr. Tuta, when he arrived at this municipal swimming pool in Siroki Brijeg, he stayed for 15 to 30 minutes, not just a few minutes. So my question to you is which is more correct? Was he there only a few minutes. Or was he there for 15 minutes to one half hour?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, but I wasn't watching -- I wasn't looking at my watch at the time. But it seemed to me as if it was between 15 and 30 minutes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And maybe it's just a matter of semantics, but in your mind, is a "few minutes" the same as a half an hour?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It depends on the occasion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And tell me what factors it would depend on, Witness ZZ?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: If it was a private meeting -- it depends on whether it was a pleasant or unpleasant event.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Understanding that every moment you were in custody during the time period that you discussed Friday was unpleasant, most unpleasant, on the occasion that you saw Mr. Tuta at the swimming pool, he didn't do anything bad to you, did he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't see him issue or hear him issue any orders to anybody, did you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You indicated --

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think we need to go into closed session for a moment, or private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We'll go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: We're back? Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After your -- after you had been transferred to Ljubuski, you stayed there for 10 to 15 days, and then were transferred to the Heliodrom; that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's also correct on the 16th of August, you were wounded in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on the day you were wounded, were you attempting to help save an HVO soldier that was in the same bunker that you were in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There was an HVO soldier in the bunker in the same location where you were wounded, though, was there not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he wasn't in the bunker. He was on the wall -- or rather, he was behind the sandbags.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you behind the sandbags with him, with this HVO soldier?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but not at the moment when I was wounded.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the moment you were wounded, the HVO soldier had already been killed; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were attempting to shore up your location and put up some wood with your hand when the bullet went through it? Is that what happened? Is that how you were wounded?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but not to shore up my position. I was making a bunker for HVO soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You indicated in your statement that you were attempting to construct a roof of the bunker to keep yourself from being hit. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that is not true at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: I had like to have the usher hand Witness ZZ a copy of his statement to the OTP in his own language.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Witness ZZ, it's on page 4. I've already had the page turned to, and there's a little red mark on the left side of the page. I'd like you to review that portion of your statement. Now, Witness ZZ, have you had a chance to review that paragraph of your statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to explain to you that I have an English translation of your statement in your own language, and there may be some differences. But could you go to that second-to-the-last sentence of that paragraph that parts out "I tried to construct the roof of the bunker..." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you go ahead and read, then, from your statement in 1998?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well. "I tried to build the roof of the bunker so as to protect it from the fire, but when I raised my hands to do that, ABiH members hit me in my right hand."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now my question was, again, were you trying to construct the roof of the bunker to keep from being shot yourself or to keep the HVO soldier who had been shot from being shot a second time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you, then, constructing the roof of the bunker to keep from being shot yourself? That's my question.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I wasn't making it for myself. I was building it for HVO men fighting on that front line so that they wouldn't be hit by the ABiH.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So in your statement when you say you constructed -- tried to construct the roof of the bunker to keep from being hit, you're not indicating yourself; you were doing it for HVO soldiers. Is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. That is my testimony.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were taken to a hospital in Mostar after you were wounded in the right hand; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you give us the name of that hospital, Witness ZZ?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the surgical hospital in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was a Croatian hospital, was it not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you were initially there for over 30 days, from approximately the 16th of August to approximately the 23rd of September. Is that a fact?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Roughly, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After that initial stay at the hospital, you were returned to the Heliodrom for approximately 10 to 15 days before you were taken back to the Croat hospital in West Mostar; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were able to stay in the Croatian hospital at West Mostar until March of 1994, a few days prior to your being exchanged and released; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you -- how were you able to stay in the hospital? Did you have a physician -- a Croatian physician that helped you stay there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have to have something signed by some doctors in that hospital to stay there rather than the Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't have any complaints in your statement, nor in your prior testimony, of any mistreatment while you were hospitalised in the Croatian hospital for that substantial period of time, do you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you being hidden out by -- in any fashion at all while you were at the Croatian hospital? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell me, please, who it was that was helping you hide out at the Croatian hospital so you would not have to return to the Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I guess my only concern is whether, first of all, whether this is relevant, especially in view of the fact that it's possible -- I don't know -- it's possible that the answer might possibly put another person in jeopardy or disclose the fact that they were assisting a prisoner. And it's on that basis that we would object. If the Court finds it to be relevant, we would ask to go into private session to take the answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Meek, you have to show us the relevance to your case.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Your Honour, this matter was spoken about, and there was testimony given Friday, direct testimony in direct examination, about his stay at the hospital in Mostar. And anything, it's my belief, I submit to Your Honour, Mr. President, that anything that this witness testifies in direct examination, I have a right to cross-examine him on those issues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, my question is that, is it necessary to know the very name of that person?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: You're probably right; I probably don't need to know the name of the person. I'll withdraw the name of the person.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Without asking you the name of the person, was it more than person who helped you hide out there in the hospital in West Mostar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'd rather not answer this question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness ZZ, with all due respect, I'm not asking for any names. I just want to know if it was one person or a greater number than one who helped you in this fashion. Just the numbers, not the names.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Several.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness ZZ, on Friday you testified, I believe, that during the time period you were in Ljubuski that there were some prisoners there from Ahmici. Did you testify to that, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And my next question would be, was this again something that other prisoners or other people had told you, or did you speak personally to these people who claimed to be from Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You testified on Friday in direct examination that while you were being held at the Heliodrom, you saw Mr. Tuta one time; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I believe if I understood your testimony, that you had this sighting of Mr. Tuta at the Heliodrom in the first weeks, week or weeks, that you went to the Heliodrom; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is, yes. It is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were at the Heliodrom, you were apparently able to look out a window to see people come and go. And that's how you glimpsed my client, Mr. Tuta; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would it be a fair statement, Witness ZZ, that while you stayed at the Heliodrom you saw many people come and go from your vantage point where you could look out the window?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So therefore, you would agree with me that it was not any sort of strange incident or out of the ordinary to see people come and go from the Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it wasn't strange to see prisoners.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Or civilians?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember seeing any other civilians but those who were detained.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the time -- on the date that you saw Mr. Tuta at the Heliodrom, would it be a fair statement that you saw him momentarily as he arrived, and then you saw him again as he exited and drove off?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I only saw him arrive and walk towards the entrance into the building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you indicated, I believe, in your direct testimony, that he was with his guards on that date?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would these be the same guards that you had indicated you saw him on the 10th day of May with in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you give me an idea as to the distance you were from your vantage point at the window of your building to the location where you say Mr. Tuta was when you observed him at the Heliodrom that one day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: About four or five metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were in the hospital in West Mostar, you saw a Croatian by the name of Misic, did you not?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I object, Mr. President. It's beyond the scope of the direct examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Meek, where are you leading us to?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: I'm leading us, Your Honour, to his stay at the hospital which he testified to in direct examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, you may continue, and let us know where is it you are leading us to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This Misic was an HVO military man, or political, if you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: He commanded an HVO unit in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He even stopped in your room and wished you a speedy recovery, did he not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: He didn't come into my room. I saw him on the stairs in the hospital building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on that occasion, he wished you well, did he not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: He did, because he thought I was a Croat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he tell you that he thought you were a Croat or are you just assuming that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Objection, Mr. President. I renew my objection as to the scope of direct, and I also would suggest this is irrelevant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Meek, we believe that this question is irrelevant. You may skip this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: I will skip this question, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness ZZ, you'll be very happy to know that I'm just about finished, so you won't have much longer. But I'd like to know if you can tell me, what month was it, if you recall, that you testified you saw Tuta, Mr. Tuta, at the Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't remember. I don't remember. At that time, time meant nothing to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask you it this way, then: You were at the Heliodrom only on three occasions; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the very last occasion would only have been a few days prior to your exchange and release; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That would have been the shortest period of time, the shortest stay at the Heliodrom; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, does that help refresh your recollection at all about whether or not you observed or glimpsed Mr. Tuta that last few days at the Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you can't recall whether it was the first time or the time in Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. between Ljubuski and the hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It was the first time, that is, after we had moved from Ljubuski to Heliodrom. It was during that period of time that I saw Mr. Tuta.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And calculating the time, we're looking at June, then, of 1993? Is that your best guess?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness ZZ, I thank you for your patience. I thank you for coming to The Hague to testify, and I wish you the best of luck in your life. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any cross-examination, Mr. Seric?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Cross-examined by Mr. Seric:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a few questions in relation to the document that the Prosecutor showed you on Friday, so if we can have D744, please, Mr. Usher. 774. Mr. ZZ, the Prosecutor had shown you this document back on Friday, and he asked you to go to Item 94, so will you please go to page 8 and tell us what the whole Item 94 is -- says. It is -- it would be your page 8, at the top.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I found it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you read the whole Item 94.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me, are we in the private session?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're right, and I apologise to you. The witness's name is mentioned here, and I apologise to you, Witness, for my omission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We'll go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. ZZ, under 94, which you saw just a moment before, is that consistent with what actually happened to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is except the date is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any re-examination? Yes, Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Very briefly, Mr. President. Re-examined by Mr. Stringer:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness ZZ, you were asked -- my colleague Mr. Meek asked you questions about your testimony in which you testified that you saw Mr. Naletilic, Tuta, at the Ministry building on the 10th of May. And I want to ask you just a few questions about that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: First of all, can you tell us, please, how long you and the other prisoners were held at this location that you've identified as the ministry in Mostar before you were taken on the buses to Siroki Brijeg?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly how much time has passed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it a matter of minutes or a matter of hours, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It seemed as if it was more than -- it was a bit more than one hour, but I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During this period of time, do you recall approximately how many opportunities you had to see the person you've identified as Naletilic, Tuta?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me, I did not get your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many opportunities did you have to see him? How many times did you see him, if you recall? Was it just one time you saw him? Did you see him on more than one occasion during this period at the ministry?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw him. I was looking at him all the time. He was present there throughout.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear him speak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I heard him speak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall who he was speaking to?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would object as being beyond the scope of the cross-examination. And I'm going to make my argument now, I must. Because in direct examination, Mr. Scott [sic] -- I apologise, Mr. Stringer. I'm apologising to both Mr. Scott and Mr. Stringer. Asked only certain questions limiting his direct examination, thereby I limited my cross-examination. And in my cross-examination, I never asked this witness anything about any conversations that he may have heard my client speak because in direct examination it did not come up. And I'm in a box now, Your Honour. I believe it's beyond the scope of the cross-examination, and I object on that ground unless I'm allowed later to re-cross.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Stringer, this question should be asked in your direct examination rather than in your re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I could briefly respond, the Trial Chamber has heard a great deal of testimony about these incidents, and perhaps I moved more rapidly through this incident in the testimony of this witness than I should have. I could certainly have dwelled on it in greater detail than I did. However, during the cross-examination, the identification was challenged, in my view, in the questions put to the witness by Mr. Meek. And I'm simply now attempting to come back to that in order to clarify or to supply additional testimony or information on the identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: But we believe that in the direct examination the conversation between Mr. Tuta and another person was not brought up. So you may skip this question, Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One final question, Witness: The time that you testified you saw Mr. Naletilic, Tuta, at the Heliodrom, are you able to tell us whether that sighting occurred before or after your injury on 16 August, 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before my wounding.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that you saw him at some point during the period after your arrival in the Heliodrom in mid-June, and then prior to -- yes, I should say sometime after your arrival in mid-June and before the time of your injury on the 16th of August. Is that the most precise that you can be in terms of the time frame?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm afraid that that is the most precise.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any questions from Judges? Judge Clark, please. Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Witness ZZ, you've given evidence which we have heard from a number of other witnesses in relation to the attack on the Vranica building. Could you explain to the Trial Chamber why it was necessary, or why you in particular felt it was necessary when you were surrendering, to take off your uniform as a military policeman for the ABiH?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that if I did not take off the uniform of ABiH, I would be killed right away or I would just die. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Was that a view that was shared, and you can only speak for yourself, but did you feel that that was a view that was shared by your colleagues?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I had a feeling that that was a view shared by my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Now, if you can move forward to the video, which I believe was shown on television on the day of the event, did you ever see that video or hear the clip of the narrative that goes with it before Friday?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: We have a transcript that we have been furnished with of what was actually said at the time that that clip was shown on television. Now, I know you're a witness, and it's not always easy to catch everything that doesn't involve you. But would you agree with the content of the narrative, that extremists had captured this building and were holding Croats as prisoners or hostages?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that was not correct at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: On the clip, ZZ, there was -- there were a series of shots I think taken at different times, but at one stage you come to a picture of a very thin man in a green uniform. He's on his own, and he has long hair; they look like dreadlocks. And then the clip goes on to a group of HVO officers and soldiers. Do you know who that man with the dreadlocks is or which army he belonged to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was with the ABiH.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Did you know who he was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Who was he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: We called him Zuba, Z-U-B-A Q.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: He kept his uniform on. Do you know what happened to him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: If I can now go to the municipal swimming pool and the works which were carried out there. You described how one day Mr. Tuta came to the pool, and you described that a man who was Jablanica had been the officer in charge at the pool. You also described a young man, who when he saw Mr. Tuta, going white with fear, and then going to talk to Mr. Jablanica. Could you elaborate on that evidence, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what you're interested in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Do you know anything about the young man who went white with fear and when he went to Mr. Jablanica, was he seeking his protection or what was the point of that evidence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I did not follow that conversation. I did not hear what was said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Thank you for assisting me.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any questions out of Judge's questions? Yes, Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I should clarify one thing, perhaps, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you testified or indicated that the videotaped footage of the Vranica is footage that you saw before last Friday when you testified. And I wanted to ask you, did you have an opportunity to see the footage more recently here in The Hague before you testified, or did you actually see the footage on television at some time in 1993 or 1994 back in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was sometime in 1994 in Bosnia-Herzegovina, in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness, for coming here. And Mr. Meek, still has a question to ask.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Your Honour, I do, out of the Judge's questions. And Mr. Stringer almost cleared it up. Further cross-examined by Mr. Meek:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness ZZ, you testified just now that you saw this footage and the audio in Bosnia-Herzegovina. Can you tell me about what year that would have been?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next question is, were you ever shown that footage again by anyone from the Office of the Prosecutor's office before you testified on Friday, last Friday?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But without the audio.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I first came to -- for proofing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you first came for proofing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you mean by "proofing"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I came here to see what was done here and what they can expect.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it last week prior to your testimony?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it subsequent to 1998 when you gave your statement to the OTP?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know a date, a month and a year, approximately? My last question.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was sometime in October 2001.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, ZZ. And again, I wish you the best of luck in life.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Witness, for coming to help us. When the usher pulls down the blinds, you may go. And we all wish you a good luck in your future life.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: At this stage, are there any documents to tender?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, the Prosecution tenders Exhibit P17.1, which is the revised Vranica videotape with audio; P17.2, the transcript of that videotape; Exhibit P30, which was the videotaped footage of the inside, the interior, of the MUP building in Siroki Brijeg. Mr. President, the witness looked at Exhibits 26.6 through 26.10, all of which were photographs which I believe are already in evidence. If not, we tender those. The witness made markings on Exhibits P20.2 and 20.11, and so we would offer those two photographs as marked. So those would need new exhibit numbers. Also, the documents, Exhibits P565.1 and P566.1. Those are two new documents which we tender at this time. The witness also looked at Exhibit 774, which I believe the Prosecution has also already tendered. But if I am mistaken, we tender that as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Stringer, I believe the videotape has already been admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Exhibit 30, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Exhibit 17.1 and 17.2, as well as 30, 26.6 to 10, they have all been admitted into the evidence already.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I believe that Exhibit 17 had previously been tendered and admitted, and then my recollection is that the Trial Chamber indicated it wished to have the audiotape, so then the full version unredacted or unedited was made by us. And if I'm mistaken, Mr. President, if it's already in, then it's in. If it's not in, we just wanted to make sure we tendered 17.1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Any objections? Mr. Seric?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Defence of Vinko Martinovic has no objections, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Meek?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: The Defence of Mladen Naletilic has no objections, Your Honours. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Those documents are admitted into the evidence. It is so decided. Well, who will deal with the next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President. Mr. Bos will be handling the next witness. I don't know what your preferences are in terms of whether you want to start now or take a slightly early break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Bos, would you please inform us about the relevance of the indictment as well as what kind of protective measures the next witness is seeking so that we could make the proper arrangement, if there's any, during the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, yes, I can do that. The next witness will be testifying -- has requested to have his face distorted and a pseudonym. And I think his pseudonym will be Witness AB, if I understand the Registry. And the relevance to the indictments are to the following paragraphs: The background paragraphs 10 and 11; the superior authority paragraphs 14, 16, and 17; general allegations, paragraph 20 and 21; count 1, paragraphs 26, 28, 31, 34(a), (b), and (d); counts 2 to 8, paragraphs 35 through 38, and paragraph 44; count 18, paragraph 54; and count 21, paragraph 57.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I guess there's no objections concerning the protective measures. Mr. Meek?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: None, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Well, we will break here, and we will resume at 11.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Bos.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm ready to proceed with the witness, if he can be brought in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Usher, would you please bring in the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Would you please make the solemn declaration in accordance with the paper the usher is showing to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You may sit down, please. Yes, Mr. Bos, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Examined by Mr. Bos:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness. Are you comfortable?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Trial Chamber has granted your request for protective measures, which means that during your testimony, your face will be -- the public image of your face will be distorted, and you will be referred to as a pseudonym. Now, the usher is going to show you a sheet of paper which has your name on it and the name of the pseudonym. I'd like you to look at that paper and confirm whether this is, indeed, your name.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you can see on the paper, you are being referred to as "Witness AB." Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: That's fine, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: May I proceed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness AB, what is your ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: Muslim.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In May 1993, did you live with your wife and your two daughters and your son in West Mostar?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's on... Well -- Witness, could you please tell the Court what happened on the 9th of May, 1993? Where were you and what happened on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: On the 9th of May, 1993, I and my family were in our flat . That evening in the northern camp, that is, on the left bank, intensive gunfire started. War, or -- as a matter of fact, I don't really know what it was. But I'm about 100 metres from the northern camp as the crow flies, so that I came out onto the balcony because I didn't know what was going on. I just assumed that there was a war being waged, that there was fighting on that side, on the left bank. Several times I went out onto the balcony, but it was night-time so that one couldn't see much. And I waited for the morning, and in the morning, we heard that there had been fighting in the camp, around the camp, and things of that sort.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was fighting whom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: Who was fighting whom? Well, I suppose the BH army and the HVO, as likely as not. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you refer to the camp, you refer to the northern barracks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: The barracks in the northern camp, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in the days following the 9th of May, did anything happen to you and your family? Did anyone came to your house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: Well, following the 9th of May, the hell started, my personal hell and my family's hell set in. At that time, we went through terrible things. The flats were broken, people were beaten. There was looting. I personally went through it all, together with my family.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, you said that -- sorry. You said that flats were broken and people were beaten. Are you talking about what you saw in the neighbourhood or what you experienced yourself or both?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: Both. I experienced horrible things during that time they entered flats, plundered, carried away. But I, in particular, experienced -- now, what was the date? It must have been two or three days later. They entered my apartment -- it wasn't broken into because I dared not lock the door. And that man entered, I knew him because I believe he lived nearby.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: His name was Muca -- I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was this man wearing a uniform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: Yes, he had an army uniform, and he was never without a weapon. He entered my flat with another two men, that is, as a matter of fact, they were outside, and then they also entered. He ordered us to go to the living room and not to move from there. He threatened us with weapons, and then he entered the children's room and our bedroom looking for something; I have no idea what. And then he took -- well, there was nothing to take, really. But he saw a CD player, and that is what he took away and left. They did not beat us. The next day, the same thing happened again, except that I heard some noise. They went upstairs -- by upstairs, I could hear somebody crying on the third floor. Later on, that is, I found that it was the third floor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did they take the next day when that same person came again? What did he take from you on that second day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: Let me tell you this first. This group which came the next day, they beat good and proper a neighbour of mine, and then they came downstairs to my place because we were the only two Muslim families in that particular building. All the others had already been expelled, and I don't really know what happened to them. But in my building were three Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Serb families, but they had left long before that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me just --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: So they came to me --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you talk about soldiers, and you've mentioned that they were wearing uniforms, were these HVO soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: I guess so. To tell the truth, I never heard -- I was -- I never had much contact with the army. I didn't take part in anything, but they all wore uniforms and carried weapons and had some insignia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please continue what happened to you on that next day.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: But this was a different group. It wasn't Muca's group. It was some other people. And they came to my place. They banged on the door. By that time, we had all removed our name plates from the doors. And I had done the same thing. And I suppose they were going from one door to the other, so they came to my place then. And at that moment, the man who I suppose was their commander or something -- I don't know -- he recognised me because we knew one another. We used to work together for the same company. I think his name was Sunjic or something else. I can't remember. As a matter of fact, his father worked with me, and his father was killed in an accident that happened in our company. And he came afterwards. He was quite younger. And when he recognised me, he turned back, and he told others, "Don't go in there." And then I went upstairs to see what had happened to my neighbour, and he was all covered in blood. Children were crying. So I helped -- I did what little I could do, and then I went downstairs to my flat again. So that was that. We didn't sleep during those days. We were constantly apprehensive, constantly on the alert expecting somebody to turn up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened toward the end of June?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: Toward the end of June, at that time those were very hard times. And we then decided -- we were quite at a loss what to do because I had three children; one daughter who was 16, 17 at the time, a younger daughter, and a son. And we then decided to leave, but we didn't know where. We simply had nowhere to go. My brother lived at the top of Avenija. So it occurred to me to go to his place. I don't really know why. Because at that time many people had been taken to camps, and I could see that my neighbours were missing, I mean those who had stayed behind. And then -- and so we went to my brother, to Avenija to seek shelter there. We were really completely at sea. I didn't know what to do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You went to your brother's place. What happened at your brother's place on the 1st of July?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: On the 1st of July, I came there with my children, and there I found my sister-in-law with her daughter. I didn't know where my brother was. He had a small summer cottage on the way to Capljina, and he had gone there. And later on I found out that he had ended up in a camp, too. But at that time I didn't know that. At that time, we were still waiting for something. And that evening, on the 1st of July, soldiers, or rather my sister-in-law saw the soldiers come through the main entrance, and then we were thinking what to do with me? But I simply didn't know what to do. And so I decided to hide under a couch. So I got under that couch somehow, and my wife lay on that couch. They came in, they searched, asked if there were any adult men. No, there aren't. So they looked around the flat, balcony, the bedroom, and left. They did not find me then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you do the next day and the day after?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: The next day, I was too afraid to stay there. But I didn't know where to go, and so my sister-in-law, my brother's wife, told me to go down to the cellar where coal is kept normally. And downstairs, we somehow arranged things and I spent the night there. I didn't sleep, but I spent the night there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can I ask why you were too scared to stay in the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: Well, I was simply afraid. Now, I didn't fear for myself. I think that at that time I was beyond fear by then. But I was afraid for my children, and I didn't know what might happen. My sister-in-law is -- her daughter, who was 17, and then my daughter of the same age and my younger daughter, and it was they I feared most for. So I decided to spend the night down there. And on the third day, they came again. And they were by the front door with a lorry, and I decided not to hide any more. That is, to simply sit there and wait.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you then put on the lorry and where were you taken to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: And then they went upstairs, and I came along, picked up a package of cigarettes, and went with them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you say "them," who were them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: Well, soldiers again wearing -- I don't know who they were. I did not know them personally. And then we got on to that lorry. They were already in it 15, maybe 20 people in it. Some of them I know. I knew, well, two or three of them, and I felt slightly relieved then. I mean, we were all going somewhere, so...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The people who were all in the lorry, were these people of Muslim ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did they take you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: We went directly to the Heliodrom.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Could the witness be shown Exhibit 20.9, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: Yes, I was brought to this building here.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Could the ELMO be raised, please. I'm not getting any picture.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We saw nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: We're not getting any image on our monitor. Just one moment, Witness. There's a technical problem. If you switch on the video channel, you'll get the image.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, with the marker could you indicate which building you were taken? And maybe we could get the whole photograph on there. I don't think we have the whole photograph on there.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Could you please circle that building with the marker which is in front of you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall what the name of that building was, how it was referred to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: It was called "prison." It's an old stone building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For how long were you kept at the Heliodrom, Witness AB?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: Well, I left the Heliodrom on the 19th of December.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So is it fair to say that if you arrived there on the -- you stayed from the 3rd of July to the 19th of December, about half a year; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: That's right, a little less. About half a year, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During this half year, were you ever taken out to perform labour?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: It was a regular occurrence in my case. I was taken to work practically every day except when after a forced labour shift, I felt ill. My pressure shot up, and then a doctor -- we had a doctor who was also an inmate, I think. And he gave me some tablets to bring my pressure down. Because it had gone up to 24 by 150, so I couldn't really keep on my feet. And that was the only time, perhaps a week or maybe two, when I didn't have to go to the front line. But all in all, I went there every day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, what kind of work did they order you to do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: Well, we mostly dug trenches, protected them with sandbags, made parapets, that is, fortified lines.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you indicate on which lines you worked, where, the various locations where you worked?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: I was on all parts of the front line, from Santiceva to Bulevar to students' hostel, Hum, Buna, towards Mostar, towards the airport, all over, all of the segments of the front line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've mentioned Santiceva Street. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many days -- do you recall how many days you worked at the Santiceva Street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: I worked for about four days on Santiceva.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this four consecutive days or were these all spread around in the period that you were staying at the Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: Four consecutive days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you recall approximately when that was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: I do not recall dates, but I think it was August. Mid-August could have been; I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please describe the work you had to do at Santiceva Street and under which conditions this -- you had to do this work?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: The Santiceva Street was hell for the prisoners really. It was a terrible situation. I know that part of town; in fact, I did not live very far from there. Also, I went to school there. And I knew that street as my own street. When I first came to the Santiceva Street, I did not know where I was. In fact, literally, you could not recognise it. So that we who had known that part of town where all surprised, even though most of the people who went there had never been there before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, I would object to the answer; it's non-responsive. The question was simply to describe the work this witness did on Santiceva Street, and we have gone on for ten lines with no description of the work he did. It's a non-responsive answer and I object on those grounds.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I believe the witness will come to that very point. And it is his first time to be in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: I did not finish.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You may continue, Witness.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: I just wanted to say in a way of introduction to what then followed. But if you asked what we did at the front line at Santiceva Street, we had -- the first night when I got there, people had been working there before, but there were two cars there. I don't know what makes. We had to pull them to a building that was in the backyard of buildings. It was not on the street. It was behind the building. And when we placed them in their positions, then we were bringing the sandbags there to build some kind of a parapet, I guess. The worst of it was, as far as my work is concerned, with several fellow prisoners, was when we had to bring to a building -- and I don't know what the purpose of it was. We were brought these bottles filled with gas, and they were filled with explosives, and it had some kind of a string attached to it. We had to light and then leave quickly. You can imagine what it was like when we were caught between -- in the crossfire. In front of us was the ABiH, and behind us was the HVO, and we were caught up in the middle. And you had to carry out all this work.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it -- do I understand you to say that while you were doing these tasks, that people were shooting around the area where you were, where you were doing this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: It was never without shooting. It was rare that there was no shooting. The shooting went on almost all the time. That was the most terrible part of it, the shooting in the location where I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, do you know for which military units you worked, for which soldiers you had to do this work?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: No. I did not have an opportunity to ask that, nor did I dare ask such questions. I simply did my work. And at a point -- at that time, when I was working, I was not interested in that. All I was interested was to try to save my life, to stay alive. That is what was important for me, simply put. But I did know the commander there. I had known him personally. But what units he was in charge of, what he was a commander of, whether that was police or not, I don't know. But I know that Braco Merdzo was in command. I knew him, and I knew him personally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, in those days that you were at Santiceva Street, were you ever at a place called the Hotel Ero?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: Hotel Ero, no, we had nothing to do there. We only entered into the basement of the Hotel Ero, or it may have been an underground garage, from the Santiceva Street. And we would make coffee. Sometimes we would stay there 15, 20 minutes to rest up, to have something to eat if we had any food and then go back to the confrontation line.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Could the witness be shown first Exhibit 11, and then Exhibit 11.6, maybe both of them. Maybe first is Exhibit 11.6, the photograph, could be placed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, do you recognise this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: That's the Hotel Ero.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So is this the building where you would stay, as you testified, in the basement of during breaks at the time you were working at Santiceva Street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: Yes, but you cannot see it from here. It is the entrance from the other street, over there. We would enter from the opposite side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So we see a street here in front of the hotel. That's not the Santiceva Street. Is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: No. This is the street, I believe it was called Mosa Pijade. I don't know what it's called now, but...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could the witness now be shown Exhibit 11, please. And I would like to have the unmarked map, so the one without the photographs. We have a copy here. That's Exhibit 11.18; I'm sorry, I thought it was Exhibit 11. If that could be placed on the ELMO, please. Now, Witness, please familiarise yourself with the map, and if you could indicate where the Hotel Ero was located on this map.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Maybe you could again with a marker put a cross where the Hotel Ero was located.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you said that you had coffee breaks in this Hotel Ero in the basement. Did you ever encounter a commanding person in that area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: Which commander? Can you please repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were at this basement, did there come a time that this man you have been referring to as Mr. Merdzo, did he come and approach you at one moment? And was there anyone else with him at that time as well?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, I object to the leading and suggestive nature of that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Well, the witness asked me to clarify a bit more what the question --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, you may proceed, Mr. Bos.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you answer the question, please, Witness.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: Yes, I did see Merdzo there. He did come there, and we were brought there. And he was in contact with the people who were there. I don't know what they were talking about. We would be on one end, and they would be on the other. I could not hear what they were talking about, nor was I particularly interested in it. But he was a regular there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see him talking with a particular person?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: No, Your Honours, I object on the grounds that it has been asked and answered. The question has been asked and answered. He asked him who he saw, he said he saw Merdzo there, and -- it has already been answered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: No, I don't think this question has been answered. The question is: Did you ever see him talking with a particular person? It's more specific.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: My objection goes to the vagueness -- the form of the question is very vague.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I think the Prosecutor is trying his best to avoid any leading questions in this aspect. Let him fish for a while. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. You may proceed, Mr. Bos.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So Witness AB, did you ever see this Mr. Merdzo talk to a particular person, and did you later find out whose name it was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was this person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: That was Naletilic, Tuta. I need to clarify that, if you permit me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just tell us the circumstances under which you saw the two talking, where you were situated, how far it was, and so please elaborate a little bit.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: We were on a break at that time, and we may have been there about 10 minutes. And then first Merdzo came. He told to the person who had brought us there, the soldier, "Take those balijas back or I'll kill them all." Then this man told him something, I guess he was also fed up because there was so much shooting going on around there. People were getting wounded or killed. And then this man came -- I did not even know that he was Tuta. I may have known of him only from newspapers, and then one of my fellow prisoners said, "You know who this is?" And he had come with two other people. And he said that he was Tuta, even though I had never seen this man before, nor did I have any contact with him in my whole life. That is how I saw him, and I never saw him again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you describe him.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: I remember well. I remember him well from that time. He was -- he had this uniform, what do you call it? Like a military uniform, camouflage, long hair, probably. I did not look very closely. I was afraid to look.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you give a few more description. You've said he had a camouflage uniform and long hair. Did you recognise anything else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the colour of his hair?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: Excuse me?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've testified that he had long hair. Can you give a few more extra details; for example, what was the colour of his hair, did he have a beard, did he have glasses, anything of that nature? Do you know a bit more?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: I think he had grey hair. And at that time, no, he did not wear glasses at that moment. Listen, at that point, if I had known that I would be in a situation where I would need to describe this man, I perhaps would have given him a closer look. But I was beside myself. I knew that it is who -- it is he that it was. And past that, I did not have much interest in anything else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you look around in this courtroom and see whether the man you saw you claim to have been Tuta, is he in this courtroom today? Could you look around and see if you identify him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: Of course I can.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please describe him for the record. Where is he seated and what is he wearing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: In the back row, third. He is wearing a suit and a tie. Sorry, in fact, he's in the middle.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: May the record reflect that the witness identified the accused Mladen Naletilic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, you said that you later on found out who this man was. Did you also find out what his military position was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: I heard about it, again, from stories. But to be honest with you, I did not know what his position was or who he was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know for which unit he served, which military unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
utterances.text: In Mostar, people were saying that this was Tuta's unit. I don't know if their name was convicts unit or something like that. As I said, these military things, I did not have enough contact to gain that kind of knowledge about names of units. And again, in the final analysis, it wasn't really of much interest to me anyway. But I heard that it was Tuta's unit, that it did exist.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, do you know whether soldiers of Tuta's unit were actually working at Santiceva Street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AB
